patient_overview.name: Alec Barton
patient_overview.description: Alec Barton is a 58-year-old warehouse worker from Toms River, New Jersey, who comes in after a recent hospital stay for a whiplash injury and ongoing heart disease. He is unfailingly polite and agreeable, nodding along with whatever is suggested, but he answers questions in short bursts and rarely volunteers much unless asked twice. He used to walk and watch his portions a couple of years ago after his heart diagnosis, but those habits have quietly faded, and his wife now does virtually all the cooking and plating at home. A dietetics student will need patience and a second or third question to get past his pleasant, surface-level answers.

demographics.occupation: Part-time warehouse inventory associate at a home-goods distribution center
demographics.residence: Toms River, New Jersey; household of 4
demographics.cultural_context: Alec grew up in a working-class South Jersey family where big weekend dinners were how the family showed love, and finishing what was on your plate was a point of pride. He never finished college and has always deferred to people he sees as "the experts" — doctors, bosses, and now his wife in the kitchen. He doesn't see himself as someone who thinks much about nutrition; that was always "her department."

secondary_diagnoses: Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging heart+coronary circulat
medical_history: Abnormal findings diagnostic imaging heart+coronary circulat since 2021
Whiplash injury to neck (2026-04 to 2026-05, resolved)
Development of individualized plan of care (2026-04-10)
current_symptoms: Occasional chest tightness when he climbs the stairs at the warehouse too fast
Gets short of breath walking from the parking lot some mornings
Stuffy nose and sinus pressure that comes and goes, worse in humid weather
Neck still feels stiff some days since the car accident in the spring
clinical_findings: Appears overweight with weight carried mostly around the abdomen
Mild nasal congestion and post-nasal drip, breathes through his mouth a bit when talking
Faint healing stiffness in neck movement, turns head slowly and carefully
Skin looks a little pale, no obvious distress at rest

medications.name: Clopidogrel 75 MG Oral Tablet

medications.patient_concerns: He doesn't really know what it's for beyond 'the heart thing,' just says the doctor told him to take it

medications.adherence: Fairly consistent, his wife sets out his pills each night

medications.adherence: Has only used it a couple of times, keeps it in his jacket pocket 'just in case'
medications.patient_concerns: A little embarrassed to use it in front of coworkers, so sometimes just sits down and waits out the chest tightness instead

supplements_and_otc: Men's multivitamin his wife bought at the pharmacy, takes it when he remembers
Fish oil capsules, started after a magazine article his wife read
Tums for occasional heartburn after big dinners

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Standard American diet shaped by his wife's cooking: meat-and-starch dinners, generous portions, not much attention to sodium or fat content
food_preferences: Diner breakfast on Saturdays - eggs, bacon, home fries
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Second helpings offered and accepted almost automatically
Salt shaker used at the table without tasting first
Fast food picked up some lunch shifts at the warehouse
Snacking on crackers or chips while watching TV at night
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Three meals a day, wife cooks dinner every night and packs his lunch; breakfast is often just coffee and a muffin before work
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly coffee in the morning, a couple of sodas during the day, modest water intake
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Used to walk the neighborhood loop most evenings after his heart diagnosis; has mostly stopped since the car accident and now mainly just does his warehouse shifts
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Light drinker, a beer or two on weekends, never smoked
nutrition_profile.sleep: Sleeps around 7 hours, occasionally restless since the accident when his neck aches

psychosocial_profile.personality: Agreeable to a fault; says 'sure, sounds good' to almost any suggestion but rarely changes his actual habits afterward
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Gives short, polite answers at first - 'fine,' 'okay,' 'not bad' - and only opens up with a second, gently persistent question
goals: Keep working at the warehouse without trouble
Not worry his wife more than she already does
concerns: Not wanting to be a bother to the care team
Worried the neck injury will slow him down at work permanently
Doesn't like talking about his heart in detail
beliefs: Thinks that since he 'already changed his diet once' a couple years ago, he's basically fine now
Believes food is really his wife's responsibility, not his
Figures if the doctor doesn't bring something up, it must not be that important
motivations: Wants to be around for his kids and grandkids
Doesn't want his wife to worry even more than she already does
Wants to keep some independence at work
fears: That he'll end up like his father, who had a major heart attack in his early 60s and was never the same afterward
Losing the ability to work and feeling useless
barriers: Low health literacy - doesn't fully understand his own lab numbers or what they mean
No control over what's cooked at home
Habits that improved a while back have quietly slipped as life got busier and more stressful
Avoids bringing up symptoms so as not to alarm his anxious wife
strengths: Willing to attend appointments and follow instructions when clearly laid out
Has a supportive household, even if it's not perfectly tuned to his needs
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Wife is attentive and does all the cooking, but tends to hover and worry, sometimes making Alec downplay symptoms to keep her calm; two grown children live nearby and visit regularly

initial_information: He says he's 'doing okay' and the hospital stay for his neck 'wasn't a big deal'
Mentions his wife does the cooking at home
Says he takes his heart pills 'pretty much every day'
discoverable_information: Admits he used to walk every evening after his heart diagnosis in 2021 but stopped after the car accident in April
Says lunch at the warehouse is often fast food or whatever's quick
Mentions he doesn't really know what three of his four medications are actually for
Says his wife packs his plate and he just eats what's given to him
Reveals the nitroglycerin spray sits in his jacket pocket most days unused because he feels silly using it at work
reluctant_information: Admits, if asked gently a second time, that he gets short of breath some mornings walking from the parking lot and hasn't mentioned it to his doctor
Mentions that his stress has crept up lately because of money being tight on part-time hours
hidden_information: His father, Walter Barton, had a massive heart attack at 61 and was never able to work again, dying at 67 after years of being housebound, and Alec is quietly terrified the same thing is happening to him right now

opportunities.learning_objective: Recognize and respond to a patient who gives short, surface-level answers
expected_discoveries: Alec's first answers to most questions are brief and minimizing
A second, specific follow-up question often reveals more detail
He is not being evasive out of distrust, just habit and low engagement with his own care
possible_patient_reactions: 'Fine, I guess.' then after a pause, 'Well, actually, there was this one morning...'
'Oh, I don't know, whatever she makes.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Assess readiness to change in a patient who has slipped from a prior maintenance stage
expected_discoveries: Alec made real changes (walking, lighter portions) after his 2021 diagnosis but has drifted back to old habits
He believes he's still 'doing fine' because he changed once before
Stress and the recent injury disrupted his routine
possible_patient_reactions: 'I already fixed my diet a few years back, so I figured I was good.'
'Guess I kind of fell off that, huh.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore household food dynamics when someone else cooks and plates meals
expected_discoveries: His wife controls almost all food decisions at home
He has limited input or awareness of sodium, portion sizes, or ingredients used
Opportunities exist to involve the wife directly in nutrition counseling
possible_patient_reactions: 'That's really her department, I just eat what's put in front of me.'
'She'd probably know more about that than I would.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify low health literacy and tailor education accordingly
expected_discoveries: Alec doesn't know what his medications are for beyond vague descriptions
He doesn't understand his cholesterol or LDL numbers
Simple, concrete language and teach-back methods will work better than clinical jargon
possible_patient_reactions: 'The doctor just said to take it, so I take it.'
'I don't really know what LDL means, is that bad?'

opportunities.learning_objective: Gently uncover a hidden fear tied to family medical history
expected_discoveries: With rapport, Alec may reveal his father's early heart attack and decline
His fear of repeating his father's fate may be driving some anxiety but also avoidance of discussing symptoms
This fear could be reframed as a motivator for sustainable change rather than something to hide
possible_patient_reactions: Changes subject quickly at first: 'Let's not get into that.'
If trust builds: 'My dad went through this. I don't want to end up like him.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Address the role of an anxious, hovering partner in the patient's self-reporting
expected_discoveries: Alec sometimes downplays symptoms to avoid worrying his wife further
This dynamic could be masking symptoms the care team needs to know about
Involving the wife constructively, rather than letting her anxiety suppress disclosure, is a key consideration
possible_patient_reactions: 'I don't like telling her when I don't feel right, she already worries enough.'
'She'd probably want to come to every appointment if she could.'
